scenes.focus: one miniature enclosed railway freight wagon is positioned by a dark-gloved investigator's hand on a weathered railway route drawing with three distinct marked locations, visually comparing known observations with an unresolved branch
scenes.camera: tight angled overhead shot of the paper rail plan on a detective's wooden table, with the one wagon token and three marked locations in sharp focus, face of the investigator completely unseen
scenes.location: a rain-shadowed private detective's office in industrial Birmingham in the 1920s
required: exactly one small dark brass freight-wagon model held between gloved fingers on the paper route
a single hand-drawn rail map with three distinct circular stop marks connected by one branching railway line, two checked points and one uncertain mark
a metal engineer's ruler and a plain mechanical drafting pen near the bottom of the map
scenes.background: old wooden worktable, worn railway ledgers, cast-metal desk lamp and rain-streaked window with distant smoke-blackened brick mills
scenes.light: focused warm amber desk-lamp illumination across aged paper and dark gloves against cool blue rainy industrial dusk
scenes.npc: one anonymous investigator visible only by dark wool sleeves and black leather gloves, no face and no other people
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: The map distinguishes recorded observations from assumptions. Only one wagon and one rail journey exist. The image never proves disappearance, witness movements, a final wagon location, or completion of the investigation.
avoid: multiple wagons, a train arriving at a documented destination, or witnesses physically appearing on the map
a stamped official declaration that the wagon disappeared or reached a secret station
recognizable face or altered canonical appearance of any selectable hero
readable invented station names, routes, times, or new witness addresses
